utterances.text: Hi, Linda. Fancy seeing you here. How long have you been shopping?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Almost an hour. I have a lot to buy. My daughter Melissa’s birthday is coming. I’m trying to get her a good gift, but I don’t know what to choose. She seems to have everything she loves.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Yeah, the same as Clara. We’ve already had bags of toys she’s no longer playing with. So this year, we didn’t buy her material things. We gave her an experience gift.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: What’s that?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: A city pass, with which she can visit 12 different attractions, including the national history museum, the science museum, the zoo, and more.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: How much is it?

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Fifty dollars per person, for a year-long pass. I bought three for the whole family.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: So you can have a different outing every month for the entire year. What a great idea!

utterances.text: Helen, busy doing anything?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Oh Kevin, I’m preparing a presentation for the city library. It’s about a girl named Tracy Woods.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: What’s special about her?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: It was an amazing story. She brought specially-trained dogs to special education schools and helped children to build confidence. She believes that dogs can help children in ways we can’t. Dogs don’t judge, and they don’t care who you are or what you look like.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: But putting dogs into a school? Aren’t they going to mess up the school?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Don’t worry. All the dogs are assessed and trained properly. There are now 40 dogs working with children aged from 6 to 18.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: I hope the children love them.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Of course they do. I’ve got some pictures. I’ll show them at my presentation tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Emily, thank you for taking time out of your busy schedule to answer a few questions.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: It’s my pleasure.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: People say you’re doing unpaid work in the new season of My Fair Lady. Is this what the show business has become?

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: No, not really. All of my acting in the new season is unpaid. But the crew is paid. This is to raise money for the post-production of the show.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: I notice you’re tried many different kinds of things: film, TV, and even theater.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: Yeah, that’s how I was trained at university. I work on anything that excites me.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Tell us about the six months you recently spent at the workshop of the Film Center.

utterances.speaker: Woman
utterances.text: It was an unbelievable experience, teaching young actors and actresses, and working with some great acting artists. It was also great to work in various labs, such as directors, writers and so on. It’s very helpful for making you a really well-rounded and active member of the film and television industry.

utterances.speaker: Man
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Emily. We look forward to your new season.
